payload:
You are Agent SECRET for Heaven Local Bridge. Work independently and actually implement, test, and commit a credential-safe GUI input design in fengie/mhw-mods.

Context:
- heaven = worker/execution Windows machine.
- heaven2 = control/credential-authority machine.
- Durable bridge source is origin/main; branch heaven-bridge is transport only and MUST NOT be merged wholesale.
- Existing worker v3 protocol chatgpt-heaven-bridge-v2, bridge files under heaven-bridge/.
- Do NOT use Remote Desktop Commander.
- Do NOT put any password/token/API key/cookie/private key/recovery code in Git, GitHub queue/results/status, logs, controller state, command line args, or test fixtures.
- Current live bridge supports gui_type but explicitly forbids secrets because queue params persist.

Goal:
Implement the strongest practical credential-safe GUI-input path that allows a secret originating on heaven2 to be typed into a GUI on heaven without the secret entering the persisted GitHub relay. Prefer a direct heaven2<->heaven local/Tailscale credential broker with ephemeral one-time handles and strict zero-persistence/redaction. Design for fail-closed behavior.

Requirements:
1. Start from current origin/main in a dedicated worktree/branch named agent/bridge-secret-safe-input (or a collision-safe equivalent).
2. Inspect existing bridge architecture/tests and preserve compatibility.
3. Implement code, bootstrap/manage support, docs, and tests. Avoid requiring cloud services or storing secrets in repo.
4. Separate control-plane requests (GitHub relay may carry only nonsecret request IDs/public metadata) from secret data-plane (direct authenticated machine-to-machine path). Use short TTLs, one-time consumption, bounded memory, explicit zeroization where practical, no secret echo, no secret logging.
5. Provide a GUI action that consumes a one-time secret handle and types it locally without returning the secret. Never accept secret plaintext through relay params.
6. If secure direct transport needs a local helper on heaven2, implement its code/config/bootstrap and document exact pairing/setup without embedding credentials. Prefer OS-native/Tailscale identity and/or locally provisioned keys protected outside Git.
7. Add threat-model notes covering replay, MITM, stale handles, logs, crash persistence, screenshots/clipboard, and privilege boundaries.
8. Run relevant unit/integration tests plus bridge gate. Do not claim live secret handling with real credentials; use synthetic nonsecret sentinel data in tests.
9. Commit your work to your task branch and push it. DO NOT merge to main; an integration agent will reconcile parallel work. In your final stdout, print exactly: branch, commit SHA, files changed, tests run/pass counts, design summary, and any unresolved blocker.
10. Clean up temporary test artifacts but keep the task branch for the integrator.
